rounds.proof_sketch: With fixed input shape [16, 16384], dim_size = 16384. Original condition: 16384 <= 256 → FALSE. Mutated condition: 16384 <= 255 → FALSE. Both take the same path (else branch), resulting in BLOCK_SIZE = 512. The mutation only differs when dim_size = 256 exactly, which is unreachable under fixed shapes.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the boundary condition from `dim_size <= 256` to `dim_size <= 255`. This only affects behavior when dim_size equals exactly 256 (original selects BLOCK_SIZE=128, mutated selects BLOCK_SIZE=256). However, the fixed input specification mandates shape [16, 16384], meaning dim_size is always 16384. At this size, both original and mutated code evaluate their conditions as FALSE, both fail the `dim_size <= 512` check as well, and both end up in the else branch setting BLOCK_SIZE=512. Since the shape cannot be modified under the testing contract, there is no value-level input that can trigger the differing code path.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed shape [16, 16384]. The mutation would only be observable with dim_size=256, which requires shape change that violates the testing contract.
rounds.recommendations: When testing block-size selection mutations, ensure test coverage includes input shapes at each branch boundary (e.g., dim_size = 255, 256, 257, 512, 513). The current fixed shape of 16384 only exercises the largest block-size path, leaving boundary-condition mutations in smaller-size branches undetectable.
